newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says 70 dead in Kurd rebel clashes.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says 70 dead in Kurd rebel clashes.

text.p: Sixty-eight Kurdish guerrillas and two members of a pro-state militia group have been killed in clashes in southeastern Turkey in recent days, security officials said on Monday.
Security forces killed 58 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas in a four-day operation, military headquarters in Ankara said in a statement.
The statement said the rebel commanders in the provinces of Erzurum and Tunceli were among those killed. It did not give the exact time or place of the clashes.
Ten guerrillas and two members of a state-paid anti-rebel militia died in a separate clash in the province of Sirnak late on Sunday night, security officials said.
The Turkish government pays and arms up to 70,000 villagers, mostly Kurds, to fight the PKK.
More than 24,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old conflict between security forces and the rebels, fighting for independence or autonomy in the southeast.

Turkish forces began withdrawing in large numbers from northern Iraq after a month-long foray into the area in pursuit of PKK rebels, witnesses said on Sunday. More than 10,000 Turkish troops streamed into northern Iraq on May 14.
